entry_state: Customer obligations explain why identical cash can support different revenue, liabilities and future service. Costing and impairment likewise require retained histories. The equipment-preparation example has introduced separate machine, sample-production and period costs; its closing statements and depreciation remain to be read.
exit_state: Equipment cost, replacement, revaluation and employee-benefit examples preserve the history needed for later measurement. Impairment now introduces an asset floor that redirects a unit's loss rather than merely clipping it. The continuation must explain reversal ceilings and what happens when all admissible allocation capacity is exhausted.
findings: Equipment available for use depreciates under the admitted consumption method while idle; sample-sale margin remains separate from machine cost.
Replacement removes old carrying value. Revaluation retains asset-specific prior loss and surplus, with direct surplus transfer separated from profit and OCI.

The pension rollforward separates employer contributions from plan-paid benefits. The initial CGU floor case assigns 5 to asset A and 25 to B after removing goodwill. No confirmed new defect in the inspected pages.
